purpose: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF LEG 4'S HEADLINE. Leg 4 found the fused path's wall advantage is mostly eliminated launches -- ~59 python-mediated launches for the baseline against one, at 6% GPU-busy on an H100. But a user can erase the baseline's launch overhead TODAY: it CUDA-graphs cleanly (4/4 attempts, both devices), while the fused path fails capture 8/8. So the race actually available to someone choosing between these implementations is D_base GRAPHED against G_base AS IT SHIPS. This is registered before the data because it can falsify leg 4's headline, and it should be run before leg 4 is published anywhere.
also_measured: Peak transient memory under FAITHFUL routing, both fixtures. F.linear saves its weight for backward, so the baseline holds every HIT expert's materialised bf16 weight across the fwd->bwd window: the old fiction gave it top_k hit experts, real routing gives ~59. Leg 1 measured this axis on the fixture now known to understate it, and memory is where this kernel's claim has always been strongest.
handicaps_registered_in_the_BASELINE's_f: A replayed graph reuses its input buffers; a real training loop would copy fresh activations in each step and the graph does not pay for that here.
The fused arm gets no equivalent optimisation, because none exists for it today.
Both make this test HARDER on gnf4, which is the direction an adversarial test should lean.

frozen_predictions.P1_graphing_helps_the_baseline_a_lot: PREDICTED: graphing gives the baseline >2x at training shape, because that is where it is 6-13% GPU-busy and makes ~59 launches. If graphing gives it little, then its host cost is not launch overhead and leg 4's mechanism is wrong.
frozen_predictions.P2_the_headline_survives_or_it_does_not: NO DIRECTION PREDICTED, and this is the point of the test. Leg 4's faithful d/g at training shape was 10.05 (4090) and 11.37 (H100). If d/g_GRAPHED stays above ~2 the advantage is real against an optimised baseline. If it collapses toward or below 1, leg 4's headline is an artifact of comparing an optimisable path against an already-optimal one, and every results doc in this leg must say so in those words.
frozen_predictions.P3_memory_favours_the_fused_arm_more_und: PREDICTED: the baseline's transient memory rises materially from fiction to faithful (it holds ~59 materialised weights instead of top_k), so memory D/G under faithful routing exceeds leg 1's figure. If it does not rise, the saved-weight mechanism is not what drives that axis and leg 1's memory story needs revisiting.

no_bars: Report-only. This probe cannot 'pass'; it can only tell us whether a published claim survives the strongest cheap attack available.
stop_rule: Whatever it shows is written into RESULTS-leg4-routed.md verbatim, including if it removes the headline. No re-running for a better number, no adding optimisations to the fused arm afterwards to even the race -- that would be a different, later experiment with its own registration.
